papers.title: A toric construction of the spectral Tate curve
papers.abstract: We develop toric geometry spectral algebraic geometry. In particular, we lift toric varieties to flat schemes over the sphere spectrum. Furthermore, we prove several rigidity and strictness results allowing us to define and produce strict group actions of flat algebraic tori. As an application, we give a construction of the Tate curve in spectral algebraic geometry. This approach lets us produce a lift of the Tate curve to $\mathbb{S}[[q]]$. We furthermore describe how to lift (arithmetic) toric stacks.

papers.title: The M\"obius Homology Laplacian for Persistence Modules
papers.abstract: Persistent homology provides a framework for studying the evolution of topological features across filtered spaces. While persistence diagrams give discrete invariants that record the birth and death of homological features, they do not directly encode analytic or geometric structure associated to persistence modules. This paper develops a spectral framework for persistent homology by introducing and studying a Laplace operator on the M\"obius chain complex, called the M\"obius homology Laplacian. M\"obius homology categorifies M\"obius inversion for persistence modules by replacing integer-valued data with vector-space-valued chain complexes. By equipping these chain complexes with inner products, we define a Laplace operator on the M\"obius chain complex whose kernel provides canonical cycle representatives for the associated M\"obius homology space. We analyze the spectral properties of this operator in two primary settings: one-parameter persistence modules and birth-death modules arising from filtrations of simplicial complexes. For one-parameter modules, we completely characterize the eigenvalues of the degree-one M\"obius homology Laplacian. For birth-death modules, we show that the trace and determinant of the degree-zero M\"obius homology Laplacian reflect the combinatorial structure of the persistence diagram.

papers.title: On p-Group Actions and Index Divisibilities
papers.abstract: We prove a mod-$ p $ divisibility result for indices of elliptic operators assuming a smooth action by a finite $ p $-group on the base manifold of dimension $ n\le 2(p-1) $ with no stationary points and which lifts equivariantly to the operator bundles. We show as one consequence that if such manifolds are spin or stably almost complex, with the group action lifting to the relevant structure, then their class in the relevant bordism theory modulo $ p $ is fully determined by one genus, and indeed vanishes for $ n<2(p-1) $. We show as another consequence that there exists no closed connected $ 24 $-dimensional spin manifold $ M $ satisfying $ {\hat{A}(M)=1}, {\hat{A}(M;T_\mathbb{C}M)=0} $, and for which there exists a smooth non-trivial action by the monster group, resolving a question of Hirzebruch.

papers.title: The Seifert--van Kampen Theorem
papers.abstract: The Seifert--van Kampen theorem computes the fundamental group of a space from an open cover by two path-connected subspaces, provided their intersection is path-connected. This article gives a self-contained account of the theorem, explains its universal-property formulation as a pushout in the category of groups, and derives several standard computations. Particular attention is paid to base points, the role of path-connectedness, and the passage from a topological decomposition to a group presentation. The purpose is expository: the results are classical, and no claim of a new theorem is made.

papers.title: A fourfold Toda bracket that is not defined, although both threefold subbrackets contain zero
papers.abstract:
We give an explicit example, in the stable homotopy groups of spheres, of a fourfold Toda bracket that is not defined although both of its threefold subbrackets contain zero. Namely, $0\in\langle
u^2,2,\eta^2angle$ and $0\in\langle 2,\eta^2,
uangle$, but $\langle
u^2,2,\eta^2,
uangle$ has no defining system in the sense of Kochman. This answers a question of Isaksen. The computational input consists only of relations from Toda's book, together with an explicit choice of null-homotopies. The same holds, in the sense of Walker, for the unstable quadruple $(
u_n^2,2\iota_{n+6},\eta_{n+6}^2,
u_{n+8})$ for every $n\ge10$. Moreover, for $n\ge10$, even Cohen's fourfold bracket of this quadruple is empty.

papers.title: Unstable Solidification
papers.abstract: We construct a solidification functor $\LH$ on condensed anima by localizing at the maps inverted by solid integral chains. A pointed connected nilpotent condensed anima is $\Hsol$-local precisely when its fundamental group admits a finite central series with solid abelian factors and its higher homotopy groups are solid. For simply connected condensed anima, we construct a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence \[ E^2_{p,q}=L_ps(\pi_qX)\Longrightarrow\pi_{p+q}\LH X \] where $L_ps$ denotes the $p$-th derived functor of the abelian solidification.

papers.title: A compact nonformal manifold with holonomy Spin(7)
papers.abstract: We construct a compact simply connected eight-manifold with holonomy Spin(7) and a triple Massey product of degrees $(3,2,2)$ that does not contain zero. The manifold is a resolution of a flat orbifold. Joyce's gluing theorem gives it a torsion-free Spin(7) structure. The resolution map factors through a quotient of $Y\times S^1$, where $Y$ is Mart\'in-Merch\'an's nonformal $G_2$ manifold. The map to this quotient has degree one, so pullback preserves a nonzero Massey pairing. On the resolution the detecting degree-two class annihilates the full indeterminacy. Simple connectivity and nonformality imply full Spin(7) holonomy. The manifold has $(b_2,b_3,b_4^+,b_4^-)=(22,10,91,27)$.

papers.title: Homotopical interpretation of directed Van Kampen
papers.abstract: We construct the Grandis model structure on directed spaces with $\Delta$-generated underlying spaces and on the full subcategory of $\Delta$-Hausdorff objects. In either setting the model structure is left proper, and its weak equivalences are precisely the maps that induce equivalences of fundamental categories in the sense of Grandis. The fundamental category functor preserves all small homotopy colimits with values in the folk model structure on small categories. For a union of two induced directed subspaces, the union square is a homotopy pushout precisely when Grandis's categorical pushout formula holds. His covering theorem gives this conclusion whenever the interiors of the two subspaces cover the space.

papers.title: Tame homotopy theory and the Goodwillie tower of the identity
papers.abstract: The purpose of this note is to provide a modern treatment of Dwyer's tame homotopy theory and extend it to non-simply connected spaces, exploiting a connection with the work of Heuts on the Goodwillie tower of the identity. As an application, we construct spectral Lie algebraic models for Hess's $r$-mild homotopy theory.

papers.title: Upper bound $2^{n}-1$ for chromatic number of orbit polytope of a small cover is attained for every $n\geq4$
papers.abstract: Davis and Januszkiewicz proved that the facets of a simple $n$-polytope $P$ which is the orbit space of a small cover can be properly coloured by $2^{n}-1$ colours. The bound is sharp for $n=2$, it is not sharp for $n=3$ by the Four Color Theorem, and it was shown to be sharp for $n=4$ by the first author. We show that it is sharp for every $n\geq4$. The polytope is obtained from the dual of the cyclic polytope $C^{n}(2^{n}-1)$ by truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$. The resolution works over an arbitrary field and gives the sharp bound $(q^{n}-1)/(q-1)$ over the field with $q$ elements. More generally, every simple $n$-polytope whose facets can be properly coloured by $k\leq2^{n}-1$ colours becomes, after truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$, the orbit polytope of a small cover with the same chromatic number $k$. We also construct, for every $n\geq4$, a simple $n$-polytope with $\chi=2^{n}-1$ which is the orbit space of both a small cover and a quasitoric manifold, and in the oriented case we obtain the sharp bound $2^{n-1}$ for every $n\geq4$.

papers.title: Explicit Bases for the Second Integral Homology of Cactus Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the second integral homology $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$ of cactus groups $J_n$. We first use Hopf's formula and Pontryagin products to obtain a smaller generating set of $H_2(J_n;\mathbb{Z})$. We then construct a detecting homomorphism to prove that these generators are linearly independent and hence form an explicit basis.

papers.title: Moore spaces, polyhedral products, and positive scalar curvature
papers.abstract: Gromov conjectured that the macroscopic dimension of the universal cover of a closed $n$-manifold of positive scalar curvature is at most $n-2$. Gromov's conjecture holds for a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 5$, provided that its fundamental group has property $(*)_m$, i.e., its classifying space is stably homotopy equivalent to a wedge of Moore spaces. We prove property $(*)_m$ for a large class of groups, including for instance the fundamental groups of closed hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups with low-dimensional nerves, pure braid groups, and many graph products thereof. As an additional application of independent interest, we show that there are finite-index subgroups of right-angled Artin groups that do not have property $(*)_m$ and can have arbitrary torsion in their (co)homology in any degree.

papers.title: Equivariant Localization for $K(n)$-Local Gromov-Witten Invariants with Applications to Gopakumar-Vafa Invariants
papers.abstract: For certain complex-oriented $K(n)$-local cohomology theories, we establish equivariant localization formulas for global Kuranishi charts and a Riemann-Roch formula. We apply these formulas to compute the genus-zero Gromov-Witten invariants of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-1)$ at odd primes, obtaining a residue formula in terms of the formal group law of the chosen complex orientation. As an application, we derive a multiple-cover formula expressing the genus-zero Morava $K$-theoretic Gromov-Witten invariants of closed symplectic Calabi-Yau threefolds in terms of their Gopakumar-Vafa invariants.

papers.title: Theories of bundles with additional homotopy conditions
papers.abstract: A homotopy between two amplified special unitary bundles and a trivialization of a tensor product give two different finite-dimensional classifying spaces. For coprime ranks $k,l>1$ the first space is a biquotient of $\SU(kl)$ and the second is a homogeneous matrix Grassmannian. We distinguish the two manifolds for every such pair by their first Pontryagin classes. For $(k,l)=(2,3)$ their eighth integral cohomology groups have orders $3$ and $21$, respectively. The same amplification maps define a dimension-drop algebra on a labelled simplex. Its skeletal filtration gives a weighted cellular complex and computes $K_0$, $K_1$ and the unit when the vertex labels have greatest common divisor one. We also compute both groups for triangles with arbitrary vertex labels.

papers.title: Topological Frobenius algebras
papers.abstract: We define in a graded and topologized setting the notions of unital/counital/biunital infinitesimal anti-symmetric bialgebras and coFrobenius bialgebras and discuss their algebraic properties. We also define in this setting the notion of a 2D open-closed TQFT. We illustrate these structures with old and new examples of geometric origin that arise in contexts as varied as symplectic topology, string topology, manifold topology, and quantum homology. The underlying vector spaces, which are typically infinite dimensional, belong to a class of topological vector spaces known as Tate vector spaces.

papers.title: Independence of homogeneous GKM manifolds and symmetric spaces
papers.abstract: Let $G/H$ be a simply connected homogeneous space of maximal rank. Then the maximal torus $T$-action on $G/H$ equips it with a structure of a Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson (GKM) manifold. We call the $T$-action $j$-independent if any $i\leq j$ pairwise distinct isotropy weights at a fixed point are linearly independent. Using weighted graphs, we show that the maximal independence of $G/H$ is $2$, $3$ or $n=\dim T$, and that the cases of $3$ or $n=\dim T$ correspond to some symmetric spaces of rank $>2$ by using the Lie bracket structure at the tangent space at identity coset. We classify all $4$-independent homogeneous spaces by studying the $3$- and $4$-cycles in the matroid of the respective root subsystem complement using Borel-de Siebenthal and Cartan classification results. In the classical $G$ cases our case study of maximal independence relies on signed weighted graphs, following the classical methods of Zaslavsky and Harari. In the exceptional simply laced $G$ cases we either present a $3$-cycle, or prove that there is none by reducing them only to those having a form $x+y=z$ for positive roots $x,y,z$ and find an affine hyperplane containing the respective root complement. As a corollary, using the results of Ayzenberg and Masuda, the lower-degree reduced rational cohomology groups of the orbit space $T\backslash G/H$ vanish.

papers.title: A bordism theory related to matrix Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Matrix Grassmannians give finite-dimensional representatives for virtual bundles of rank one and vanishing first Chern class. We use them to study two groups of labelled manifolds. A choice of stable normal framing gives framed bordism of $\BSU_{\otimes}$ and an integral Pontryagin--Thom description. Forgetting the framing gives a quotient defined by the boundary relations for labelled, stably parallelizable manifolds. The forgetful map is surjective with torsion kernel. Both rational bordism rings are polynomial on explicitly labelled spheres, one generator in each even dimension at least four. We compute the characteristic numbers of their products and show that each sphere generator spans an integral direct summand in its own degree.

papers.title: The universal Euler characteristic and Burnside group for definable groupoids
papers.abstract: We introduce the universal Euler characteristic of orbit space definable groupoids, a class of groupoids containing cocompact proper Lie groupoids as well as translation groupoids associated to proper definable group actions. We show that every additive and multiplicative invariant of orbit space definable groupoids with an additional local triviality hypothesis arises as a ring homomorphism applied to the universal Euler characteristic. This in particular includes the $\Gamma$-orbifold Euler characteristic introduced by the first and third authors when $\Gamma$ is a finitely presented group. For definable groupoids, where the object and arrow spaces as well as the structure maps are definable, we also introduce a Burnside group which is an analog of the classical Burnside ring associated to compact Lie groups and, for a transitive groupoid with compact isotropy, admits a partial multiplication.

papers.title: The 2-local homotopy types of G_2-gauge groups
papers.abstract: We determine the 2-local homotopy types of G_2-gauge groups over S^4.

papers.title: GKM Theory for Manifolds of Isospectral Matrices in Lie Type D
papers.abstract: We study the manifold $Q_{\Gamma, \lambda}$ of isospectral real skew-symmetric matrices with a prescribed sparsity pattern determined by a graph $\Gamma$. The compact torus $T^n$ acts naturally on $Q_{\Gamma,\lambda}$ by conjugation, and this action can be studied using GKM theory. We prove two results about this manifold and its GKM graph. The first theorem describes how the GKM graph of $Q_{\Gamma, \lambda}$ is obtained from the GKM graph of the corresponding manifold $M_{\Gamma, \lambda}$ of isospectral Hermitian matrices. The second theorem shows that equivariant formality of $Q_{\Gamma,\lambda}$ implies equivariant formality of $M_{\Gamma,\lambda}$, whereas the converse fails.

papers.title: Homotopy exponents of polyhedral products
papers.abstract: We study Moore's conjecture and homotopy exponents for polyhedral products. For $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ where each $A_i$ is finite and has torsion-free homology, we prove that if $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ is rationally hyperbolic, then it has no homotopy exponent at any odd prime. Under the additional hypothesis $\Sigma A_i$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite-type wedge of simply-connected spheres, we show Moore's conjecture holds for $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$. We also give criteria such that, for a large family of polyhedral join products, the associated polyhedral products are rationally hyperbolic, mod-$p^r$ hyperbolic for all but finitely many primes, and have no homotopy exponent at all but finitely many primes.

papers.title: Integral cohomology of classical Artin groups: spherical types $A,C,D$ and affine types $\widetilde B,\widetilde C,\widetilde D$
papers.abstract: We determine the additive structure of the integral cohomology groups with trivial coefficients of the Artin groups in the spherical families $A_n,C_n,D_n$ and the affine families $\widetilde B_n,\widetilde C_n,\widetilde D_n$. We first compute the integral cohomology of braid groups by algebraic methods and then use the Salvetti complexes to express the cohomology of the remaining families in terms of these computations. The resulting descriptions apply in every admissible rank. For each family, we establish cohomological stabilization and show that the integral cohomology groups contain no elements of order $p^2$ for any prime $p$. We also give uniform generating series formulas describing the stable integral cohomology in terms of that of the braid groups.

papers.title: Fractal Hyper-Trees I. Combinatorial foundations: definition, enumeration, invariants, morphisms and the algebra $\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb H\oplus M_3(\mathbb C)$
papers.abstract: Fractal Hyper-Trees (FHTs) are hypergraphs organized in levels: each level consists of disjoint connected clutters, and every edge strictly contains each lower component that it meets. Connected clutters and Schr{\"o}der hierarchies are the two extreme cases. Every FHT decomposes uniquely into the children of its top component, which carry smaller FHTs, and a host, an arbitrary connected clutter on these children. This gives an exact recurrence by size and depth and a species equation; the counts begin 1, 1, 4, 23, 231, 16947, 490083358 and are exact through nine vertices. Four interior moves (fusion, fission, aggregation, explosion) connect the FHTs on a given vertex set; every FHT on at least two vertices descends to the star by moves at distance at most one from the root, and $\kappa-1$, with $\kappa$ the number of edges, is its distance to the star. For FHTs with automorphism group $S\_4$, twisting the real group algebra by the sign character gives $\mathbb{C}\oplus\mathbb{H}\oplus M\_3(\mathbb{C})$, the finite algebra of Connes' description of the Standard Model. Conversely this algebra determines the group up to isomorphism and the class of a real 2-cocycle. The axioms select neither the group nor the twist: with the twist fixed as the sign of the action on the vertices, the algebra occurs exactly when $\mathrm{Aut}\,F\cong S\_4$ and some automorphism is odd on the vertices, at every size $v\ge4$. Every finite group is the automorphism group of a flat FHT, and every faithful action on a finite connected simplicial complex is rigidified into a flat FHT with the same reduced integral homology. All computations are deposited and their kind (exhaustive, sampled, exact or numerical) is stated.

papers.title: A homotopical enhancement of Neisendorfer's algebraic models
papers.abstract: We give an $\infty$-categorical enhancement of Neisendorfer's equivalences between the homotopy categories of rational simplicial sets, commutative dg algebras (cdgas), cocommutative dg coalgebras (cdgcs) and dg Lie algebras (dgls), where these objects have respective hypotheses of connectedness, nilpotency and finite type. We do so by proving that linear duality is a partial Quillen equivalence between weak finite type connected cdgcs and cdgas, and that Quillen's Chevalley--Eilenberg adjunction is a partial crossed derivable equivalence between cdgcs and dgls, a concept we introduce in this paper to axiomatize precisely the behavior of this adjunction.

papers.title: The Art of Toda Brackets: A Journey through the Homotopy Groups of SO(n) in degrees 23-29
papers.abstract: One of the fundamental aims of the present book is to provide a reference for the computation of unstable homotopy groups using methods developed by the Toda school. The Toda bracket serves the art of constructing homotopy liftings and extensions of maps. The theory of Toda brackets is fundamental to the study of composition relations among homotopy classes. Appendix~A.3 brings together all known results on the $2$-primary components of unstable homotopy groups of spheres obtained primarily through Toda brackets, with explicit generators. Appendix~A.2 explains the conventions used to name the generators. The book presents calculations, with explicit generators, of the $2$-primary components of $\pi_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ for all $23\leq i\leq28$ and all $n$, together with selected calculations in degree $29$; (two possible group structures remain for $\pi_{28}(\mathit{SO}(11))$). The odd-primary components in the range considered can be computed with little additional effort, essentially by consulting the relevant entries in existing tables. As a further check, we examine our result for $\pi_{23}(\mathit{SO}(9))$ using the unstable Adams spectral sequence.We also give some geometric applications.

papers.title: Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three
papers.abstract: The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence. A divisibility calculation for the mod-$3$ Moore spectrum supplies a lift to a finite spectrum with a degree-$144$ self-map. The resulting iterates have nonzero image in the height-two detector of Carrick and Davies.

papers.title: Embeddable matrix-algebra bundles
papers.abstract: A unital embedding of a bundle of complex matrix algebras in a trivial matrix algebra bundle of coprime multiplicity determines two complementary factors. We recover from them an integral virtual special-unitary bundle of rank one. This gives a proof of the stable classification by $B{\rm SU}_{\otimes}$ that allows torsion in the cohomology of the base. At fixed core rank $k$, the telescope of matrix Grassmannians with complementary ranks $l^N$ is the homotopy fibre of $B{\rm PU}(k)\to B{\rm Aut}(M_k\otimes M_{l^\infty})$. Thus unital UHF triviality detects exactly which cores admit coprime finite-dimensional embeddings. We determine the least stage on even spheres and on four-dimensional Moore spaces. A rank-three example over $S^6$ first embeds in $M_{12}$ and represents a unit whose clutching gives a higher twist over $S^7$.

papers.title: Topological entropy and Burau representation
papers.abstract: Let f be an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of the disk D, P a finite invariant subset and [f] the isotopy class of f in D\P. We give a non trivial lower bound of the topological entropy for maps in [f], using the spectral radius of some specializations in GL(n,C) of the Burau matrix associated with [f] and we discuss some examples.
